findings.title: Federated recovery-code creation drops the credential metadata
findings.body: When user storage accepts the update, it receives only a UserCredentialModel containing the type and JSON list of raw codes. The generated-at timestamp and user label already present on credentialModel are not propagated; unlike the local fallback, a storage provider therefore cannot recreate the same RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. The added test provider demonstrates this by storing the current time and no label, so a configured label is later returned as null. This makes recovery-code metadata inconsistent between local and federated storage and loses the originally generated timestamp/label.

findings.title: The federated test provider accepts recovery codes indefinitely
findings.body: The recovery-code validation branch only checks whether the submitted value occurs in the persisted list. It never removes the matched code or records it as used, so the same recovery code succeeds on every login. getCredentials reconstructs all codes as unused as well. The new integration test performs only one successful login, so it passes despite violating the one-time recovery-code requirement. Persist consumption atomically and add a second-login assertion showing that reuse of the same code is rejected.

findings.title: Recovery credentials returned by the test storage lose their persisted ID
findings.body: updateCredential assigns the persisted recovery credential an ID at line 195, but getCredentials reconstructs a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel from the raw values without copying that ID. The returned credential consequently has no ID, or an ID unrelated to the backing record. Callers use credential IDs for credential-management operations, and the recovery authenticator uses the returned ID when cleaning up an exhausted credential, so those operations cannot address the stored recovery-code record. Preserve myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() on the reconstructed model and cover exhaustion/removal in the integration test.
